s: Managed point-to-point queue with at-least-once delivery, visibility timeouts, and dead-letter parking.
w: Producers send messages (≤256KB); consumers poll (long-polling reduces cost) and 'hide' messages via visibility timeout while processing - delete to ack, or let timeout redeliver. Redrive policies move repeatedly-failing messages to a DLQ. FIFO variant adds ordering/dedup within groups. Scale is effectively unlimited per API quotas.
use: Decoupling web tier from slow work (emails, images, exports)
Buffering spiky writes before durable DB updates
Job processing where order doesn't matter but reliability does
Retry semantics for flaky downstream APIs via DLQ + replay
avoid: Strict global ordering across all messages (FIFO only orders within message groups)
Huge payloads - store object in S3, send pointer (extended client pattern)

props.visibility_timeout: How long a received message stays hidden before redelivery

size.messages_per_sec: ~10k sustained per queue before batching strategies matter

pat.d: Poison messages park in DLQ with alarms; engineers replay after fixes.

pits: Duplicate deliveries are guaranteed eventually - make consumers idempotent with dedupe keys
Visibility timeout shorter than processing = double-processing storms - size it > p99 handler time
tips: At-least-once + idempotency pairing is THE expected answer combo
